newsitem.title: JAPAN: Super Dry puts sparkle in Asahi Breweries earnings.
newsitem.headline: Super Dry puts sparkle in Asahi Breweries earnings.

text.p: Japan's Asahi Breweries Ltd on Tuesday unveiled a triple record in its group sales, current and net profits for calendar 1996, helped by robust sales of its flagship "Super Dry" brand beer.

The nation's second-ranked beer maker said that on a group basis its sales grew 11 percent to 1.21 trillion yen ($9.9 billion) and net profits rose 25 percent to 8.23 billion yen ($67.4 million). It also enjoyed a nearly 40 percent jump in current profits.
All these figures rose to record levels for a second consecutive year, a company spokesman said.
"We are now seeing a good trend of rapidly growing sales. I don't think this trend will change this year," he said.

Asahi's good earnings results were in contrast with those of longtime sector leader Kirin Brewery Co Ltd, which in February showed a triple decline in its sales, current and net profits for calendar 1996.
Kirin suffered a 2.3 percent drop in its group sales to 1.60 trillion yen ($13.1 billion), while its group net profits dropped 14.2 percent to 34.39 billion yen ($281 million).
Lacklustre sales of Kirin brand beers -- Lager and Ichibanshibori -- allowed Asahi to raise sales of its mainstay Super Dry brand.

Third-ranked Sapporo Breweries Ltd on Monday reported group sales for the period almost flat at 665.51 billion yen ($5.45 billion) but a nearly 60 percent jump in group net profit to 3.81 billion yen ($31.2 million).
Asahi predicted its bull run would continue this year and said another triple record was likely in its earnings results.
It expects group net profit to rise 21.5 percent to 10 billion yen ($81.9 million) and group sales to rally further to 1.3 trillion yen ($10.6 billion).
Kirin, meanwhile, forecast a slight rise in sales to 1.64 trillion yen ($13.4 billion) this year, with group net profits also rising to 36 billion yen ($295 million).
In January, Kirin fell behind Asahi in shipments for the first time in 44 years.
Asahi captured a 38.3 percent share of the domestic market, edging out Kirin, with 37.2 percent. Sapporo's share was 19.0 percent and Suntory Ltd trailed with 5.6 percent.
Asahi's rise to the top was largely due to a robust 42 percent year-on-year rise in sales of its Super Dry beer. ($1=122 yen)
